name: Missouri
overview: Under Missouri law the county collector offers land with delinquent taxes at a public auction each year on the fourth Monday in August, starting at 10 o'clock, at or near the courthouse; the collector may also run it online at the same time. After payment the collector gives the buyer a certificate of purchase rather than a deed. The owner has an absolute right to redeem during the following year by paying the amount due plus interest at the rate in the certificate, not more than ten percent a year, and the right to redeem ends when the buyer gets the deed.

counties.how_to_bid: Bidders must be Missouri residents aged 18 or over (out-of-state bidders appoint a Missouri resident as agent) and give the Collector a signed, notarized bidder's affidavit stating they owe no delinquent property taxes; businesses must be registered in Missouri. Show Missouri ID to get a bid number: numbers are issued only the week before the sale and stop at 9 AM on sale day. The sale starts at 10:00am in the Assembly Room of the Administration Building in Hillsboro and bidders must be present. Properties go in newspaper order (1st, then 2nd, then 3rd offerings), the minimum bid is the taxes and sale expenses due, and the highest bidder wins. Pay at the Collector's office within 2 hours after all properties have been offered; failure to pay brings a 25% fine. The eligible property list is posted on the Collector's website in June.

counties.how_to_bid: Lands and lots with taxes delinquent for 3 years are offered at public auction, with the list published in the Jefferson City News Tribune for three consecutive weeks before the sale. Buyers or their representative must be present; non-residents of Missouri may not bid unless special arrangements are made with the Collector before the sale. Buyers sign an affidavit that they are not delinquent on any tax payments (available at the Collector's office or at the sale site just before the sale). Bidding begins at the taxes, penalties and sale costs, and the total purchase price is due at the Collector's office immediately at the close of the sale by cashier's check, bank draft, cash, money order or personal check. The Collector mails a certificate of purchase; the owner may redeem within one year from the sale date.

counties.how_to_bid: Buyers must be present to bid. Registration is on the day of sale from 8:00 a.m. in the Collector's office, Room 103 of the Courthouse, where bidders complete an affidavit that they are not delinquent on any tax payment. The sale is a public auction with an opening bid covering all taxes, interest and charges; the purchaser pays the Collector immediately at the end of the sale and receives a Certificate of Purchase. Non-Missouri bidders must appoint a Lincoln County citizen as agent and consent in writing to the Circuit Court's jurisdiction. There is a one-year redemption period without possession. Properties are advertised in the Lincoln County Journal and Elsberry Democrat from the second week of July.
